name: Weiser State Forest Greenland Tract
note: Weiser State Forest's Greenland Tract, off US 209 near Williamstown: two drive-in motorized roadside sites (G001 on Radar Road, back-in for vehicles up to 34 ft on a steep gravel driveway; G003 on Chestnut Road) plus two hike-in tent sites, in forested uplands. No water, hookups, toilets or trash service (carry in, carry out). Permit and reservation always required; district office 570-875-6450. --Claude

field_notes.Booking: A permit and reservation are always required, on the Pennsylvania State Parks and Forests reservation site or 888-PA-PARKS. Check-in and check-out 3 pm; campers must vacate for at least 48 hours before returning.
field_notes.Fees: State forest motorized roadside campsite (a DCNR state FOREST program, not a state park): $10/night PA residents, $15/night non-residents, reserved through ReserveAmerica; 7-night limit.
field_notes.Sites: Weiser State Forest's Greenland Tract (off US 209 near Williamstown) has two drive-in roadside sites: G001 on Radar Road beside the AT&T (PP&L) Trail, back-in, max vehicle length 34 ft on a 34-ft gravel driveway at a severe grade, site 60 ft; and G003 on Nevin Slusser/Chestnut Road, back-in 25-ft driveway (Tent Site only). G002 and G004 are hike-in tent sites. Up to 10 people per site.

name: Putnam Pond Campground
note:
Possible issue with mosquitos.  Marsh nearby.
DEC, near Lake Champlain at the edge of the Pharaoh Lake Wilderness; the sites on the pond itself (R1-R9) are reached by boat or on foot. --Claude

field_notes.Booking: ReserveAmerica, up to 9 months ahead, same day included; DEC's 2026 summary sets a 1-night reservation minimum here. A permit runs at most 14 nights, and from July 1 through Labor Day only 14 cumulative nights are allowed at any campground. Register by 9 pm on the first night or the site is re-rented. Remote sites R1-R9 on the pond are boat-in (8 and 9 also on foot), with outhouses and no potable water.
field_notes.Fees: $18 a night; non-residents +$5 a night; $7.25 reservation fee. No hookups. DEC's 2026 campground summary, read 2026-10-12; five other DEC campgrounds charged exactly their summary fee on the booking site for 2027 nights.
field_notes.Sites: DEC lists 72 sites; ReserveAmerica sells 70, of which R1-R9 are boat-in or walk-in. Of the 61 drive-in sites, 16 are listed at 30 ft, 29 at 20 ft and 16 with no length.

name: Five River Campground
note: Private campground on the Shavers Fork in the Cheat River watershed at Parsons; Sites 225, 227, and 230 are listed as waterfront. During Pickin' in Parsons (from July 25 into early August) camping is for festival attendees only. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Limited tent camping Memorial Day to Labor Day. Restrooms/showers closed for the 2026 season; they reopen May 17, 2027.
field_notes.Booking: Book online through the campground's Bonfire booking page ('CLICK HERE TO VIEW CAMP MAP & BOOK NOW'). Rates cover 2 adults and 2 children; $5 per extra person per day; early check-in or late check-out $20. Cancellation: $5 a night if at least 72 hours out, else one night plus $5 a night. Sites not guaranteed. During the Pickin' in Parsons bluegrass festival (late July - early August) camping is only for festival ticket holders.
field_notes.Fees: Five River: rates $30-55 a night for 2 adults and 2 children. Read 2026-10-15.
field_notes.Sites: 190 full-service RV and camper sites on grass, plus tent camping.

name: Delaware State Forest Campsite O017 White Deer
note: Delaware State Forest motorized roadside site O017 (White Deer, Owego area) along PA 402 about 2 miles north of I-84. One shaded pull-in site on a long gravel driveway, limited to 2 vehicles; the entrance drive is not plowed. No water, hookups, toilets or trash service (carry in, carry out). Permit and reservation always required; district office 570-895-4000. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Open year round on the booking site; state forest roads are not plowed, so winter access is not guaranteed.
field_notes.Booking: A permit and reservation are always required, on the Pennsylvania State Parks and Forests reservation site or 888-PA-PARKS. Check-in and check-out 3 pm; campers must vacate for at least 48 hours before returning.
field_notes.Fees: State forest motorized roadside campsite (a DCNR state FOREST program, not a state park): $10/night PA residents, $15/night non-residents, reserved through ReserveAmerica; 7-night limit.
field_notes.Sites: A single roadside site, O017 White Deer (Owego loop), along PA 402 about 2.5 miles south of US 6 (2 miles north of I-84). Pull-in on a 300-ft gravel driveway; site 50 x 50 ft, shaded, 15-ft overhead clearance. Limited to 2 vehicles. No max vehicle length is given, and the booking site files it under Tent Site only.

name: E016 Fivemile Meadow
note: PA State Forest dispersed meadow campsite; not on a water body.

field_notes.Booking: A permit and reservation are always required; reserve online or at 888-PA-PARKS. Check-in and check-out 3 pm; campers must vacate for at least 48 hours before returning.
field_notes.Fees: State forest motorized roadside campsite (a DCNR state FOREST program, not a state park): $10/night PA residents, $15/night non-residents, reserved through ReserveAmerica; 7-night limit.
field_notes.Sites: A single roadside site, E016 Fivemile Meadow (Edgemere loop), on Five Mile Meadow Road just south of PA 739, about 5.8 miles north of Silver Lake Road. Pull-in, max vehicle length 30 ft; site 30 x 25 ft with a 105-ft gravel driveway, 15-ft overhead clearance, partial shade.

name: Christopher Run Campground
note: 7.5/8.5★/9  Note that the campground's "lakefront" sites are on the beach, and the beach is open to anyone who is staying at the campground. --AWH  Reserve by phone/email request form (540-894-4744, deposit required) --Claude

Booking: min stay 2 nights on weekends (Memorial Day - Labor Day), 3 on holidays

field_notes.Booking: Reservation by phone (540-894-4744), email or the website's request form ('a reservation request and does not guarantee a reservation'); one night's deposit (three on holiday weekends), due within a week of booking. 'There is a 2 night minimum for campsites on weekends between Memorial Day and Labor Day, a 3 night minimum on all holidays.'
field_notes.Fees: 2026 (Apr-Oct): 30A water + electric $45, 30A full / 50A W+E $50, waterfront 50A $55, 50A full $60; no hookup $37.

name: Sugarloaf Mountain Recreation Area site# SL 1A
note: Large waterfront site w/shelter, picnic table, fireplace, trash can. --AWH

field_notes.Booking: Reservations are required and are made only by calling the Sand Hills State Forest office, (843) 498-6478, during office hours (Mon-Fri 8 am-12 pm and 12:30-4 pm). Campers must camp in the reserved site.
field_notes.Fees: Rate for shelter site SL 1A; a reservation runs from 11 am to 11 am the next day.
field_notes.Sites: The largest shelter (fireplace, picnic table, trash can), on Mountain Road beside SL 1B, looking toward Mountain Pond; across the road from the nature trail and a restroom. Generators are allowed.

name: Sugarloaf Mountain Recreation Area site# SL 1B
note: Large waterfront site w/shelter, picnic table, fireplace, trash can. --AWH

field_notes.Booking: Reservations are required and are made only by calling the Sand Hills State Forest office, (843) 498-6478, during office hours (Mon-Fri 8 am-12 pm and 12:30-4 pm). Campers must camp in the reserved site.
field_notes.Fees: Rate for shelter site SL 1B; a reservation runs from 11 am to 11 am the next day.
field_notes.Sites: A smaller shelter (fireplace, picnic table, trash can), on Mountain Road behind SL 1A, looking toward Mountain Pond; across the road from a restroom. Generators are allowed.

name: Sugarloaf Mountain Recreation Area site# SL 2
note: Large waterfront site w/shelter, picnic table, fire ring, trash can.  Next to pier. --AWH

field_notes.Booking: Reservations are required and are made only by calling the Sand Hills State Forest office, (843) 498-6478, during office hours (Mon-Fri 8 am-12 pm and 12:30-4 pm). Campers must camp in the reserved site.
field_notes.Fees: Rate for shelter site SL 2; a reservation runs from 11 am to 11 am the next day.
field_notes.Sites: Shelter with picnic table, fire ring and trash can, the one closest to the pier on Mountain Pond, on Mountain Road. Generators are allowed.

name: First Landing State Park Campground
note: Numerous beachfront sites, but vegetation and dunes may block water view. --AWH A 23-ft motorhome fits the 27 EW-30ft sites; the 36 EW-50ft sites are for RVs 32-50 ft only and the 45 EW-20ft sites take rigs only to 20 ft (DCR, read 2026-10-21). --Claude

field_notes.Season: Winter 2026-27: the C, D, G and H loops run through the night of Dec 6 and the campground is closed until March 2027; Read loop is already closed and Collier runs only Nov 20-29.
field_notes.Booking: 'First Landing allows guests to reserve specific campsites.' Reserve online or at (800) 933-PARK.
field_notes.Fees: $43 a night for a site with electric and water (Virginia residents); non-residents $49. The $32 sites without hookups are tent-only. The same price every night of the week. Plus tax and a $5 transaction fee. DCR's fee table (effective 2025-05-12), read 2026-10-12.
field_notes.Sites: 205 sites: 45 electric/water for tents, pop-ups and RVs to 20 ft (20-amp); 27 electric/water to 30 ft; 36 electric/water for RVs ONLY 32-50 ft long; 75 no-hookup tent-only sites; 22 group tent sites (44-65). A 23-ft rig fits only the 27 EW-30ft sites.

name: Shenango Recreation Area
note:
COE campground on Shenango River Lake. Sites on a peninsula; many are right on the water. --AWH
recreation.gov describes 'over 300 campsites' (318 bookable), many with 30- or 50-amp electric; reservation only, bookable on the day of arrival. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Golden Loop (#1-26) and Old Duck Loop (#192-225) stay open until November 30 (2026 notice).
field_notes.Booking: 'The campground is reservation only. Reservations can be made on the day of arrival.' Two camping units per site: one wheeled unit and one tent, or two tents.
field_notes.Fees: Peak season (2026-05-08 to 2026-09-23): standard non-electric $24, standard electric $34, and two further non-electric rate templates at $30 and $38. Off-peak: non-electric $18, electric $20 (the $38 template is $34). Same tables 2025-2028.
field_notes.Sites: recreation.gov describes 'over 300 campsites' and lists 318 bookable ones (214 standard non-electric, 81 standard electric, 23 RV electric), all back-in apart from one. Listed lengths run mostly 45-60 ft, but the campground warns that 'the maximum vehicle length indicated on the site description is actually the total length of the site', so they are not rig limits.

name: River Forks Park & Campground
note: Locally managed campground on a peninsula in Lake Lanier.  Many of sites are directly on the water.  --AWH  Hall County (local government) park on Lake Lanier at 3500 Keith Bridge Rd, Gainesville: 40,000-sq-ft beach, boat ramp, fishing pier, paved roads. The six Timberline glamping tents book separately. Winter 2026/27 reservations not yet released: the county may lay new water lines (county notice). --Claude

field_notes.Booking: Hall County's Itinio reservation site (behind a human check). Office Mon-Fri 8 am - 7 pm, Sat-Sun 10 am - 7 pm; the campground is gated.
field_notes.Fees: RV sites $30/night for up to 4 campers and 1 vehicle; extra campers and vehicles are charged at the park. All 27 RV sites open on Monday Oct 12 2026 were $30 (county reservation site). Tent sites $24.
field_notes.Sites: 47 RV sites with water/electric per the county's feature list (the same page's prose says 63, which seems to include the 10 water/electric tent sites and the 6 glamping sites); 10 tent sites; 6 Timberline glamping tents book separately on ResNexus.

name: Burton Family Farm
note:
49-acre farm near Fredericksburg with a pond.  --AWH
Sites 1, 3 and 10 are two-wheel-drive; Hipcamp marks sites 6, 8 and 9 "four-wheel drive recommended", and the 1.5-mile road in is tight for a wide rig.  --Claude

field_notes.Booking: Instant-book on Hipcamp, up to 12 months ahead, 1 to 29 nights.
field_notes.Fees: Host's nightly price, the same on all ten site listings; Hipcamp's service fee ($6.21 on a $35 night) comes on top.
field_notes.Sites: 19 drive-in RV/tent sites in an open field around the pond, one side backing to woods; Hipcamp gives RVs to 55 ft (sites 8 and 9 to 45 ft). Hipcamp marks sites 6, 8 and 9 'four-wheel drive recommended', the others two-wheel drive or unmarked.

name: Delaware State Park
note: Heavily wooded campground in four areas linked to the lakeshore by hiking trails. Area C (sites 101-157) closed from October 4, 2026 for a construction project (ODNR notice 9/22/26); ReserveOhio blocks it through April 2027. --Claude

field_notes.Season: In winter only part of sites 1-100 is sold (about 20 open in November 2026 and January 2027); sites 101-214 are blocked November-March.
field_notes.Booking: Reservations required, up to six months ahead online or at (866) 644-6727. Every listed site is web-bookable with a 14-night maximum on ReserveOhio.
field_notes.Fees: Every RV site is electric: $39 a night, the same on a Saturday (June 2027); off-peak (November 2026, January 2027) $35. Plus tax and a $6.50 reservation fee per reservation. ReserveOhio's prices read 2026-10-30.
field_notes.Sites: 203 web-bookable electric sites (ODNR: 214, four with ADA features) in four wooded areas, all back-in, rated for camping units 42-88 ft (most 45-57). Area C (sites 101-157) closed from October 4, 2026 for a construction project; ReserveOhio still blocks it through April 2027. Two domestic pets per site.

name: Jesse Owens State Park - Sand Hollow Campground
note: The northern no-fee area of the park: a gravel road up the east shore of Horse Run Lake and on into the woods, with sites strung along about 2.5 km. Some sit at the water; the far ones are a long walk from it (a 2022 Campendium reviewer at site 81 puts it at about 1.5 miles). Boat ramp at the south end of the lake. Former AEP ReCreation Land. ODNR gives no length; a 2021 Campendium reviewer with a 26-ft trailer found the sites 'very unlevel'. --Claude

field_notes.Season: ODNR: 'generally April 1 to mid-December'; the close date is that wording, not a posted date.
field_notes.Booking: No-fee, first come, first served; campers self-register on site.
field_notes.Fees: No-fee primitive area.
field_notes.Sites: ODNR gives no site count or length and says 'no pad'. Camper reports only: about 82 sites (Dyrt 2024), numbered at least to 84. 26-ft trailer at site 43 (Campendium 2021: 'very unlevel. Suited mostly for tents, vans and very small campers'), 22-ft trailer at site 84 (Campendium 2024), 21-ft Class B at 50-51 (Campendium 2021), 36-ft fifth wheel (Campendium 2020). Pick a site on arrival; not all suit a 23-ft motorhome.

name: Lake Loramie State Park
note: Premium electric sites line Lake Loramie at the campground's north-east point (016-039) and the channel along its west and south sides (097-120); several sites have courtesy boat tie-ups. --Claude

field_notes.Booking: 'Reservations may be made up to six months in advance online or by calling (866) 644-6727.' 14-night maximum on ReserveOhio. In the off-season (sampled November 2026 through mid-March 2027) only 19 units are sold: 14 electric sites (045-049, 087-091, 131-134, 152), premium electric 016 and four tent sites; the full loop reopens by mid-April.
field_notes.Fees: Electric sites $37 a night; premium electric sites near the water $39; full hookups $50; the same on a Saturday (June 2027). Off-peak (November 2026, January 2027) electric and full-hookup $33, premium electric $35. The non-electric and premium non-electric sites ($27 / $31) are tent-only, so they don't set the RV base. Plus tax and a $6.50 reservation fee per reservation. ReserveOhio's prices read 2026-10-30.
field_notes.Sites: 156 web-bookable RV sites: 73 electric, 41 premium electric (near the water, electric only) and 42 full hookup (4 lakeside), almost all back-in pads of 45-50 ft, plus 3 pull-throughs of 50-70 ft; 14 more non-electric sites are tent-only. ODNR counts 120 electric (40 premium), 42 full-hookup and 15 non-electric sites. Several sites have courtesy boat tie-ups. Three ADA Cedar Cabins (no pets) sit inside the campground.

name: Strouds Run State Park
note: The park's concession, Strouds Run Rentals, runs the campground. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Rates are posted for every month: in season April 1 to the first Sunday in December, off season the first Monday in December to March 31.
field_notes.Booking: First come, first served with self-registration envelopes at the entrance; only the group camp and two camper cabins take reservations, through the concession (Strouds Run Rentals). 14 nights at most in any 30 days.
field_notes.Fees: $20 a night April 1 to the first Sunday in December, $15 the rest of the year (sites 19 and 20, with a shelter, $25 / $20). First come, first served with self-registration envelopes; the park's concession, Strouds Run Rentals, runs the campground. Read 2026-10-12.

name: Tionesta Recreation Area
note: USACE campground below Tionesta Dam along Tionesta Creek (Pittsburgh District). Reservation required, on recreation.gov only. 124 back-in full-hookup sites (63 with 50-amp), listed for rigs of about 41-75 ft. A few sites (e.g. 46, 48) back up above the creek; not step-to-water lakefront. --Claude

field_notes.Booking: 'All campers must have a reservation in order to camp. Reservations need to be made before arrival.' Reservations can be made up to the day of arrival (cutoff 0 days). 14 nights in any 30 consecutive days at the project. Check-in 2 p.m., check-out noon.
field_notes.Fees: Standard electric (full-hookup) sites $46 a night in recreation.gov's 2026, 2027 and 2028 peak-season rate tables; the only off-peak rate on file ($37) is for April 2024.
field_notes.Sites: 124 standard electric campsites, all full hookup; sites 69 and 71 are accessible sites for Access-pass holders. Listed max vehicle length runs 41 to 75 ft by site, most 48-66 ft. Every site is listed back-in on gravel. One wheeled camper and one tent per site, two vehicles maximum, no parking on the grass.

name: East Branch Campground
note: USACE campground on a wooded hillside near East Branch Clarion River Lake (Pittsburgh District). Reservable on recreation.gov only; 21 30-amp electric RV sites, 2 non-electric and 3 tent-only sites plus 4 cabins. Steep terrain; recreation.gov allows RVs of 20-40 ft depending on the site, five pull-throughs; 13'4" powerline clearance on the camp road. Not lakefront. --Claude

field_notes.Booking: 'WE CANNOT TAKE RESERVATIONS. RESERVATIONS CAN ONLY BE MADE THROUGH Recreation.gov.' 14 consecutive nights, 14 in any rolling 30. A 1-night minimum is marked soft. Check-in 4 p.m., check-out 3 p.m.
field_notes.Fees: RV electric sites $30, non-electric $20, tent-only $15, cabins $55, the same in recreation.gov's 2026, 2027 and 2028 rate tables.
field_notes.Sites: 26 campsites (21 RV electric, 1 RV non-electric, 1 standard non-electric, 3 tent-only) plus 4 cabins. Permitted RV/trailer length runs 20 to 40 ft by site (three electric sites cap at 20 ft); sites 19-23 are pull-through. Overhead power-line clearance on the camp road is 13 ft 4 in.

name: Tracy Ridge Campground
note: Allegheny NF ridge-top campground, a base for the Tracy Ridge trail system about 5 miles above the Allegheny Reservoir; concession-run (Allegheny Site Management). Reservable online in summer, with some first-come sites and a first-come fall season; no hookups, vault toilets, hand-pump water in loop E; the dump station is closed (2026). Back-in sites fit RVs ~25-60 ft. Not on the water. --Claude

Booking: min stay 2 nights on weekends, 3 on holidays

field_notes.Booking: Reserve on recreation.gov; some sites are always first-come, and the 2026 rate table runs a first-come, first-served season from September 9 to December 16. Weekend reservations 2 nights, holiday weekends 3. 14 nights in any 30. Check-out noon; fees paid by 2 pm by envelope.
field_notes.Fees: 2026: $12/night for a standard non-electric site in every season (group loops $75). Fee covers two vehicles and one wheeled camping unit; $5 per extra vehicle.
field_notes.Sites: The catalog lists 54 standard non-electric family sites (35 reservable, 19 first-come) plus reservable group loops; the description says 'over 70' sites. Max vehicle lengths 25-60 ft, all back-in. Each site has a picnic table, fire ring and tent pad.

name: Twin Lakes Campground
note: Allegheny NF campground at spring-fed Twin Lake (not the reservoir), eight miles southeast of Kane, with a swimming beach and fishing piers; run with the Friends of Twin Lakes. 50 family sites, 15-amp electric at the lower sites, vault toilets, dump station. Camping by donation (2026); request a site by phone (814-389-3019). A railroad underpass on the FR 191 entrance limits vehicles to under 10 ft tall: use the Dahoga Road entrance from Wilcox, which has no height limit. Near the lake, not lakefront. --Claude

field_notes.Season: 2026: open from March 26; in fall, weekends only from the last weekend in September to the last weekend in October (depending on campground hosts).
field_notes.Booking: Request a site from the Friends of Twin Lakes by phone, 814-389-3019 ('We will do everything in our power to hold the site you requested'); recreation.gov says its availability grid does not reflect availability and that first-come sites are available.
field_notes.Fees: 2026: 'Donations Only!' - camping is by donation to the Friends of Twin Lakes (100% goes back to Twin Lakes).
field_notes.Sites: 50 family campsites (picnic table, fire ring, tent pad), electric at the lower sites, plus double and group sites. Catalog max vehicle lengths 20-40 ft (most 25-35), a dozen pull-throughs. A railroad underpass on the FR 191 entrance limits vehicles to under 10 ft tall; taller campers use the Dahoga Road entrance from Wilcox, which has no height limit.

name: Hearts Content Recreation Area
note: Allegheny NF campground beside the Hearts Content old-growth area and Hickory Creek Wilderness, run by concessionaire Allegheny Site Management. 26 single sites with RV spurs (listed 25-45 ft) plus a group site; vault toilets, hand-pump water, dump station, no hookups. Open May 1 to Oct 26, reservable on recreation.gov, and every site also first-come. Not on the water. --Claude

field_notes.Booking: 'Reservations are accepted for all campground sites from May 1 to Oct. 26. All campground sites are also available as first come, first served.' Up to 6 months ahead on recreation.gov or 877-444-6777; recreation.gov closes booking 4 days before arrival, the Forest Service page says at least 3 days ahead. 14 nights per rolling 30 days. Fees are paid within 30 minutes of arrival.
field_notes.Fees: Single site $12 a night (includes two vehicles and one camping unit; $5 per extra vehicle); lean-to shelter sites $14; group site $80.
field_notes.Sites: 26 single sites plus 1 group site; two singles have lean-to shelters. recreation.gov lists max vehicle lengths of 25-45 ft (most 30-40); driveway type not listed.

name: Dingmans Campground
note: NPS concessionaire campground on federal land within Delaware Water Gap National Recreation Area, on Route 209 at Dingmans Ferry. Book direct through the campground's own Campspot link, not Recreation.gov. Riverfront sites on the Delaware are tent-only (no vehicles); the 35 RV sites are in the forest, set back, with 20/30/50-amp electric and water (no sewer; dump stations at the two bathhouses), back-in, rigs to 50 ft; forest boondock sites also take RVs. Dry campground, no generators, no cell service. Usually open late April to early November. Senior/Access passes 50% off up to 2 nights, 10% military. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Operator: 'we are usually open late April to early November'; the 2026 season closes 11/1.
field_notes.Booking: Online booking on Campspot ('Camping Reservations for Holiday weekends require a two-night minimum stay'). Cancel 7+ days out for a refund less $10; none after.
field_notes.Fees: Forest Tent/Boondock sites (no hookups; the operator sells them as 'Tent / No Amenity RV Site') $46 a night, 20-amp + water Forest Tent/RV sites $50, 20/30/50-amp + water RV-only sites $52; first four people included, $10 per additional person. Tent-only river sites $50-62. Campspot adds a small processing fee. Read 2026-10-20 on the current rates page, which carries the 2026 closing date (11/1).
field_notes.Sites: 23 riverside tent sites, 78 forested tent and boondock sites (the boondock ones take RVs) and 35 RV-ready sites with water and electric. The 20/30/50-amp RV-only sites take 'rigs up to 50 ft with slide-outs on both sides'. 'All of our RV sites are back in only.'

name: Little Buffalo State Park
note: DCNR state park campground near 88-acre Holman Lake. Reservable via the PA reservation system; 46 sites, 30 of them with water and 50-amp electric (2 of those full hookup, back-in), and a dump station, plus camping cottages and a lodge. Sites sit south of the lake, not lakefront. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Approximate: DCNR says mid-April through mid-October.
field_notes.Fees: $20 a night for a Pennsylvania resident (modern campground, showers), $24 on Friday, Saturday and holiday nights; electric +$7. Non-residents +$5 a night; $6.50 transaction fee per reservation or registration; designated pet sites +$2. DCNR's statewide price table, read 2026-10-12; the booking site charged the same for 2027 nights.
field_notes.Sites: DCNR: 'The modern campground with 46 campsites'. The booking site lists 30 Modern Electric (2 of them full hookup), 12 Modern Non-Electric and 5 walk-to sites, plus camping cottages and a lodge. Max vehicle lengths 20 to 55 ft (most 30-50); 4 electric sites are pull-through.

name: Denton Hill State Park (Nine Mile Loop)
note: DCNR state park campground (Nine Mile Loop) along Nine Mile Run, operated by the Denton Go concession under DCNR. Currently 10 rustic back-in gravel RV sites with electric (DCNR says 11); flush toilets and warm showers in the Adventure Center. Reservable online through Denton Go, not ReserveAmerica. One of PA's highest parks; max RV length not published outside the booking engine. --Claude

field_notes.Booking: Run by the Denton Go concession, not on the state parks' ReserveAmerica system (DCNR: 'Currently, this park has no reservable facilities'). RV sites book through Denton Go's Firefly Reservations page; phone (814) 754-9013.
field_notes.Sites: Denton Go says there are currently 10 RV sites, all rustic back-in gravel pads along Nine Mile Run; DCNR describes the Nine Mile Loop as 11 sites. Site-specific RV size limits are only shown in the Firefly booking engine.
